An ESPN [[2013 NBA Draft]] outlook ranked Carter-Williams as the top point guard prospect and #8 prospect overall.[http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Michael-Carter-Williams-6262/ Draft Express][http://nbadraft.net/players/michael-carter-williams NBA Draft.net][http://insider.espn.go.com/nbadraft/results/top100/_/year/2013 Chad Ford's Top 100 - 2013] ==Early years== Carter-Williams attended [[Hamilton-Wenham Regional High School]] in [[South Hamilton, Massachusetts]] as a freshman. He was 5'9" as a freshman, he led his team and conference in scoring with 20 points per game. He transferred to the boarding school [[St. Andrew's School (Rhode Island)|St. Andrews School]] in [[Barrington, Rhode Island]] where he lived in a dormitory during his final three years of high school.http://dailyorange.com/2010/12/family-guy-basketball-roots-run-deep-for-syracuse-signee-carter-williams/ In his three years as a starter, he averaged 25.4 points per game.http://www.suathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=9464 As a senior he averaged 23.2 points, 8.3 rebounds and 5.5 assists per game. He committed to attend Syracuse and play on the basketball team after his sophomore season in high school.http://www.newenglandrecruitingreport.com/news/article/1092/CarterWilliams-Big-East-Bound.php He visited colleges in the August after his sophomore year in 2009 and received scholarship offers from Syracuse, Providence, Virginia Tech, Florida State, Virginia, Notre Dame, and Clemson among others. He played on the same AAU team as top-rated NBA prospect Kentucky center Nerlens Noel.http://sujuiceonline.com/2012/02/05/nerlens-noel-michael-carter-williams-syracuse-basketball/ ==College career== Carter-Williams had eight double-double games (points-assists) in the 2012–13 regular season. He did not have a double-double game in 2011–12.
